title: What Does Machine Learning Learn from Numerical Calabi--Yau Geometry? A Controlled Study on the Fermat Quintic
abstract: arXiv:2602.07834v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study polynomial regression of numerical metric errors on the Fermat quintic. A known hypersurface volume-ratio identity gives the exact reference $C-\log p_4$ relative to the induced Fubini--Study metric, where $p_4=\sum_i|z_i|^8$ on unit-normalized homogeneous coordinates. We optimize algebraic metrics at degrees $6,8,10,12$ while preserving finite Fermat symmetry, then fit their remaining logarithmic volume-form error. Regression splits and bootstrap draws keep the five roots of each sampled line together, with all compared teachers evaluated on common clouds. Warm-start replication correlations exceed $0.9997$ at $k=8,10,12$. Across degrees, source-derived modes fall short of target-specific fits, including in a post-hoc quartic check, but outperform random spans of matched rank in the tested libraries. translated_title: 机器学习从数值卡拉比–丘几何中学到了什么？——费马五次超曲面上的受控研究
translated_abstract: 我们研究费马五次超曲面上数值度量误差的多项式回归。一个已知的超曲面体积比恒等式给出了相对于诱导 Fubini–Study 度量的精确参考 C − log p₄，其中 p₄ = Σᵢ|zᵢ|⁸（在单位归一化的齐次坐标上）。我们在保持有限费马对称性的前提下，优化次数为 6、8、10、12 的代数量度，然后对其余的对数体积形式误差进行拟合。回归划分与自助抽样始终将每条采样直线的五个根保持在一起，且所有被比较的教师模型均在公共点云上进行评估。在 k = 8、10、12 时，热启动重复实验的相关系数超过 0.9997。纵观各次数，源自源的（source-derived）模式均不及目标专属拟合——包括在事后四次多项式检验中也是如此——但在所测试的库中优于同秩的随机张成。两个独立的、保持对称不变的随机 k = 10 初始点，其残差相关系数为 0.768–0.803，而它们所拟合的三次模式相……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文以费马五次超曲面为受控实验平台，利用精确已知的体积比恒等式（C − log p₄）作为解析基准，首次定量揭示机器学习对数值卡拉比–丘度量误差究竟学到了什么：拟合高度可复现（相关系数超过 0.9997），所学模式虽逊于目标专属拟合却显著优于同秩随机基，证明回归确实捕捉到了真实且可迁移性有限的几何结构。
en_tdlr: Using the exact volume-ratio identity (C − log p₄) on the Fermat quintic as a controlled analytic benchmark, this study quantifies what machine learning genuinely learns from numerical Calabi–Yau metric errors, showing that warm-start fits are highly reproducible (correlations >0.9997) and that their learned modes, while falling short of target-specific fits, outperform random spans of matched rank.
